findings: The answer does not invent a source-defined insertion API; it explicitly chooses insert-after with sentinels as the testable candidate contract.
The core four-pointer invariant is stated directly and then derived as replacement of one bidirectional adjacency with two.
The Java implementation is complete and compilable, and the fixture checks both forward and backward traversal so a missing prev update cannot hide behind one-direction tests.
Complexity is correctly conditional: O(1) only when the insertion position/anchor is already known, while index/value lookup adds O(n).
Ownership and concurrency behaviors are surfaced as implementation boundaries rather than source facts.
